clue.text: Having no success makes French leader sick!

indicators.note: the leader of the word French is its opening letter

parts.note: someone ailing is unwell, sick

explanation.surface: An exclamation that failure makes the head of France ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To be failing is to fall short again and again, getting nowhere in an effort.

clue.text: Declines sound paving material

parts.note: something that flags weakens or declines
a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: A noise that drops in a road-building context.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstone is a flat slab of stone used for paths and floors.

clue.text: Survey the cricket, perhaps, without parking

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word's letters are wrapped round the second

parts.note: a cricket is one example of an insect
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Watching a game of cricket without a place to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' suggests the sport; it is the chirping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine or look over carefully.

clue.text: It's immature to be tense

definitions.meaning: a verb tense for incomplete past action, such as was going

explanation.definitionFit: Something flawed or unfinished is not complete; in grammar the term names the past continuous form.

clue.text: Singing for pleasure?

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a short choral song and joyful delight.

clue.text: A plot is set out in a marginal note

indicators.note: the letters of the words are laid out afresh, set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A storyline is explained in a note written in the margin of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges the letters of A PLOT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostil is an old word for an annotation written in the margin of a text.

clue.text: Not against making an enemy

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of the words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Not being opposed somehow creates a foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges the ten letters of NOT AGAINST.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an opponent or adversary.

clue.text: Round up catch for painting

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for catch is read upwards

parts.note: a trap catches its prey

explanation.surface: Gathering everyone up so they can be caught for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TRAP into PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s style of abstract art using optical illusions.

clue.text: Some won't rest lest they lose support

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people keep going for fear of losing backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'they lose support' as the definition, but that phrase cannot stand for the answer; only 'support' does, with 'they lose' part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame that holds up a table top or platform.

clue.text: Making a deal with America would be a bloomer!

parts.note: a lot is a great deal
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A trade agreement with the USA would be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake; here it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, so a flowering plant.

clue.text: Russell's work "The Moralist

parts.note: the Irish poet George Russell wrote under the pen name AE; with the possessive that gives AE'S
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A title of a book by Russell, apparently called The Moralist.
explanation.walkthrough: George Russell, the Irish poet, signed his work 'AE'; the 's is kept as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek fabulist's tales each end with a moral, so he is the classic teller of improving lessons.

clue.text: Markedly green in outlook?

parts.note: extra can mean especially or markedly, as in extra careful
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is notably inexperienced in their views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests naivety, but it is the heraldic colour VERT; the definition is a playful one: an outward-turned personality.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert is an outgoing person, one whose attention is turned outward toward people and the world.

clue.text: Drink if apprehensive about blunder

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word's letters surround the second's

parts.note: shy here means wary or apprehensive
to err is to make a mistake, blunder

explanation.surface: A suggestion to have a drink if one is nervous about making a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain, a common aperitif.

clue.text: In a stage presentation it creates a stir

indicators.note: In tells us the following word goes inside the rearranged letters
a fresh presentation of the words a stage shows their letters arranged differently

explanation.surface: Something in a theatre production causes excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presentation' rearranges A STAGE to AGATES, and 'In' puts IT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitating something stirs it up; one who agitates causes a commotion.

clue.text: After a bad beginning the answer is forgiveness

indicators.note: After says the answer's word comes behind the opening pieces
the beginning of bad is its first letter

parts.note: a solution is an answer

explanation.surface: After starting poorly, being pardoned is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is formal release from guilt or sin.

clue.text: Striking centre-spread that's over the top

parts.note: workers who are striking are out

indicators.note: the centre of the word spread is its middle pair of letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper's eye-catching middle pages are too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre-spread' looks like a magazine's middle pages, but it asks for the centre of SPREAD, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, from French, means unconventional to the point of being shocking or excessive.

clue.text: One who should disclose nothing, but will tell

definitions.text: One who should disclose nothing, but will tell

parts.words: One who should disclose nothing, but will tell
parts.note: a person bound to keep customers' affairs secret, yet whose job title in a bank is teller

explanation.surface: Someone sworn to secrecy who will nonetheless blab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tell' suggests betraying secrets; a bank's cashier is called a teller.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank employee who serves at the counter is a teller and must keep account details confidential.

clue.text: Approaches about sanction limits

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word's letters surround the second

parts.note: one who comes approaches
to pass a bill is to sanction it

explanation.surface: Moves toward the boundaries of a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sanction' could mean a penalty; here it means approve.
explanation.definitionFit: The compass of something is its range or extent, so its compasses are its bounds.

clue.text: The man with a touching system for getting rich

definitions.text: The man with a touching system for getting rich

parts.words: The man with a touching system for getting rich
parts.note: the legendary king whose touch turned everything to gold

explanation.surface: A man with a moving scheme to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' suggests emotional; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phrygian king of myth was granted the golden touch.

clue.text: Occasions when everybody can be choosy

definitions.text: Occasions when everybody can be choosy

parts.words: Occasions when everybody can be choosy
parts.note: times when the whole public gets to choose, namely by voting

explanation.surface: Moments when everyone is permitted to be fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: Polls are when voters choose their representatives.

clue.text: Put thoughts into words -—- fast

definitions.meaning: to state or voice an idea
speedy, as a fast train or delivery

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to articulate an idea and, as an adjective, rapid or nonstop.

clue.text: There's many a cheat in Burgundy

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
a con is a swindle, a cheat

explanation.surface: A remark that plenty of swindlers are found in the Burgundy region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burgundy' is the wine, not the region or the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a red or white wine from the Mâconnais district of Burgundy.

clue.text: Cats lie all over the place in Spain

indicators.note: all over the shop means scattered in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cats lounging everywhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the' rearranges CATS LIE, and 'place' doubles as the start of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Castile is a historic kingdom and region of central Spain.

clue.text: Nagging a top man with financial obligations

parts.note: a captain, abbreviated CAPT, is the man at the top
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A complaining boss who is in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Captious means fault-finding, always raising petty objections.

clue.text: The company with extreme views can appear heartless

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
Red is a label for someone of extreme left-wing views

explanation.surface: A firm with radical opinions can seem cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' suggests cruelty; here it means with the core removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cored apple has had its middle taken out.

clue.text: Granny interrupts "That's silly?"

indicators.note: interrupts means the word for granny breaks into the other

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
Nan is a familiar word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A grandmother cuts in to say something is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or foolish.

clue.text: The price of freedom

parts.note: read literally: the sum paid to have a captive set free

explanation.surface: A slogan about what liberty costs.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like a patriotic cliché about sacrifice; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper demands this payment before releasing a hostage.

clue.text: The male representative is a dope

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: Calling a male politician an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests a fool; it is a drug, cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is cannabis, often slangily called dope.

clue.text: Look again at cut-back in army personnel weapon

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: back says the word for cut is read from right to left

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a mine is an explosive weapon

explanation.surface: A review of a reduction in the number of soldiers and arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-back' looks like a staff reduction, but it splits into a word for cut turned 'back'; RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regular crossword stand-in for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something a second time is to inspect or review it once more.

clue.text: Started to drop off about one

indicators.note: about means going around, so the letters for drop off surround the one

parts.note: to shed is to let fall, drop off
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone began to fall asleep at around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop off' suggests falling asleep, but it means SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that shied started or jumped aside in fright.

clue.text: See a novel use for cinders

indicators.note: a novel use means a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Finding an inventive purpose for the ashes from the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or make out.

clue.text: Have the company of law-men going by ship

parts.note: a posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A sheriff's posse travelling by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess is to own or hold.
